prize_parts.citation: for the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube observatory, opening neutrino astronomy

statement.case_for: IceCube is a discovery made by nature and not by a model: a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice measured a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at energies far above anything covered by earlier neutrino prizes, and later work has added the TXS 0506+056 blazar, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane. That is the kind of clue from nature that I want a prize to reward. The existence of the flux is robust across several analysis channels and is consistent with KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD, so the claim does not rest on the still-modest source associations. It also bears on the origin of cosmic rays, a question that has been open for a century. On attribution, B029 is the only shortlisted candidate where every member who proposed names (Pearce, Olsson and I) proposed exactly the same trio, which counts for something when the committee must in the end name people.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that IceCube is a collaboration of hundreds, so any three names under-represent the work, and the Baikal and AMANDA pioneers, whom Spiering partly represents, complicate the credit. The astrophysical interpretation is also incomplete: most of the diffuse flux has no identified origin, and Olsson's 'absolutely sure' standard for source associations is not yet met. Finally, B029 has thin opening support (three rankings, with Olsson at 7), whereas B012 was ranked by seven of eight members, including two first places. A prize that most of the committee can live with is not the same as one a few champion, and I should not pretend otherwise.

responses.point: Pearce ranked IceCube first as an instrument-driven discovery, with decades of calibration and systematics control behind the diffuse-flux claim, and notes that the discovery claim does not depend on the weaker source associations.
responses.response: I agree, and this is why I put B029 first in the preferred configuration. I would add one qualification to your own caveat. The citation should rest on the diffuse flux and the opening of the window, not on TXS 0506+056 or NGC 1068, because those would pull in different people and a lower significance. I also push back gently on your framing of the Higgs as a lesser case: your own B039 ranking (fifth) used Della Negra where I used Jenni, and that disagreement between the two of us on a single attribution is itself an argument that B039 is harder to name than B029.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first as a textbook measurement method with 1e-18 uncertainty, independent reproduction in many labs, and a clean two-name credit (Katori, Ye).
responses.response: I take the attribution point seriously: Katori and Ye is the cleanest configuration on the list and I have no quarrel with it. My reservation is one of kind. A clock is an extraordinary instrument, but its most valuable promised payoffs (varying constants, dark-matter searches, a redefinition of the second) are still ahead, so I am being asked to reward the tool before the discovery it enables. I have not ranked it, and I want to be honest that this is partly my own bias toward results about nature. That said, I would not block it, and I have named it as an alternative because the breadth of support from you, Lindroth and Pearce is something the committee cannot ignore.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked topological insulators (B057) first for the clean Z2 mechanism and the HgTe edge-channel measurement, while acknowledging that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are missing and that the 2016 prize leaves uncertain room.
responses.response: I respect the mechanism, but you have put your finger on exactly what worries me. You, Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce all flag the missing BHZ credit, and Kane-Mele-Molenkamp is a prize in which the theorist of the experimentally realised material is not named. Add the 2016 overlap and I think B057 is the candidate where attribution is least settled among the well-supported ones. I would want to hear from you whether you think the Z2 classification alone, independent of the HgTe prediction, carries the prize.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first as a clean theory-and-experiment story that revealed new states of matter, tunable and reproduced by many groups, while noting that credit among the theorists and the pairing mechanism are unresolved.
responses.response: I find the prediction-then-confirmation structure attractive, and it is closer to my idea of physics than most of the quantum-information candidates. My worry is timing. The pairing mechanism is still debated, the discovery is eight years old, and Mehlig and Johansson both say recognition may be early. IceCube, by contrast, has a secure central result and an open astrophysical interpretation, which I regard as the more comfortable position for a prize. I would not oppose B036 in a later year.

responses.point: Johansson ranked circuit QED (B051) first and Cirac-Zoller-Blatt (B010) second as foundations of quantum information, and noted the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize.
responses.response: I ranked B010 last of my eight, so we disagree. The ion-trap control side overlaps with the 2012 prize, and your own note that B010 is a compound of ion gates and lattice simulation, overlapping with B026, is my objection too. On B051 you raise the right caution about rewarding the same field twice after 2025, and I would add that the credit rests on a theory proposal and two experiments within the same year, so the discovery itself is harder to separate from the platform.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a three-person prize for a collaboration of hundreds, and how to treat the Baikal and AMANDA pioneers beyond Spiering.

Whether the evidence on the origin of the diffuse flux (a few source associations, limited independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD) is strong enough for colleagues who want an interpretation as well as a detection.
Whether B012 should be paired with a second part; the union limit of three people makes a Katori-Ye part plus a full IceCube trio impossible, so I cannot propose both.
The Higgs attribution (Gianotti, Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) is genuinely contestable and I rely on recollection of leadership roles, not verified detail.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. None of the credited names for the shortlisted candidates is a supervisor, mentor or frequent co-author of mine; my main connections (David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet) are in string theory and are not tied to any shortlisted ballot.
